claims.statement: A deployment composes its plugin tree from `dsh.profile.bundles`, an explicit ordered list applied layer by layer over the entry list with no transitive resolution; a later layer cannot remove or override an earlier layer's insert, so two bundles inserting one composition entry id is a boot failure rather than a merge.

Every composition entry id in this workspace has exactly one owning bundle patch: `telemetry` is inserted only by the dsh-telemetry patch, `github-issue` only by the dsh-github-issue patch, `memo` and `ui-memo` only by the dsh-memo patch, `ui-memo-settings` only by the dsh-client-ui-memo-settings patch, and `openwiki-visualize` only by the dsh-openwiki-visualize patch.

One owning bundle per entry id is what lets any subset of the suite be installed together: the dsh-memo patch inserts only the `memo` and `ui-memo` rows and deliberately omits `telemetry` and `github-issue`, because it formerly inserted the `github-issue` row itself and naming every package then failed the boot with `duplicate loader entry id: github-issue`.

Five workspace packages declare `dsh.bundle` with their own `cordis.patch.yml` and list that patch in `files` so it ships in the tarball, while `@zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo` declares `dsh.client` but no `dsh.bundle` and therefore ships only `lib`.

`@zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo`'s browser panel is activated by a row that the dsh-memo bundle inserts by name, so `dsh plugin add @zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo` reports it as a plain dependency rather than a profile layer — expected for a `dsh.client` plugin — while the package must still be named explicitly for that row to resolve.

A profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` sets `autoInstallPeers: false`, so an install brings in only the packages named on the command line; installing `@zhangj1164/dsh-memo` alone leaves the `github-issue` and `ui-memo` rows unresolvable and the loader fails the boot with `Cannot find package '@zhangj1164/dsh-github-issue' imported from …` and the same error for `@zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo`.

The full memo suite is installed by naming all five packages in one command: `dsh plugin --profile web add @zhangj1164/dsh-telemetry @zhangj1164/dsh-github-issue @zhangj1164/dsh-memo @zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo @zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo-settings`.

`@zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo-settings` carries its own bundle that inserts the single `ui-memo-settings` row, so it installs as a profile layer independent of the memo bundle, but each settings page is registered inside `ctx.configForms.whileServed(...)` for the `memo` and `github-issue` namespaces, so a deployment that does not serve those namespaces shows no page and no error.

`@zhangj1164/dsh-openwiki-visualize` owns one entry id for both halves: the host service is the package body and the browser half is discovered from the same manifest's `dsh.client` declaration, so one bundle layer installs and removes the service and its right-Sidebar tab together.

Each inserted row's `config` block supplies deployment-overridable defaults rather than fixed behavior — for example telemetry `maxEventsPerQuery: 500`, github-issue `repoUrl` plus the default-off intake parameters, memo `repoUrl` with `provider`/`model` deliberately unset so analysis follows the deployment's `agentDefaultModel`, and openwiki-visualize version floors, port, and registry URL.

`verify-bundle-entries` reads every workspace package whose manifest declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, extracts inserted entry ids with a targeted line scan (comments stripped with quote awareness, no YAML parser), throws when a declared patch is missing or inserts no id, and fails when one patch repeats an id or when two bundles insert the same id.

A shared entry id whose patches both record the exclusion is reported and allowed instead of failing: the check requires the literal marker `not both` plus the id itself as a standalone token whose neighbouring characters are not `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, so `github-issue;` satisfies it, `github-issue-x` and the reordered phrase `do not enable both` do not.

The bundle-entry gate's limit is deliberate: it can only observe the bundles this repository ships, so a deployment that enables two mutually exclusive patch layers through its own profile is outside the repository and remains a documented constraint rather than a gate failure.

`verify-bundle-entries` is scheduled in the `check-all` gate aggregate without a build dependency because patch files are source, as is `verify-publish-guard`, while the artifact-reading gates `verify-package-exports` and `verify-client-bundle-id` declare `needs: ['build']`.

`scripts/publish-guard.mjs` refuses to publish a manifest with a `workspace:` range when the packer is not pnpm and fails closed on an unidentified packer; a git install is unaffected because neither npm nor pnpm runs `prepublishOnly` on install, and `verify-publish-guard` fails any workspace package whose `workspace:` ranges do not wire that guard at the repository's own path.

`scripts/tests/bundle-entries.spec.ts` pins the gate's parsing and collision rules — indent variants, commented-out rows, a quoted id containing `#`, an empty patch throwing, `mentionsExclusion` requiring both marker and bare id, and `findCollisions` accepting a documented shared id while rejecting an undocumented one and an intra-patch repeat — while the workspace-wide no-duplicate assertion lives in the gate itself; `packages/client/ui-memo-settings/tests/entry.spec.tsx` pins the two `whileServed` namespaces and that nothing registers while they are unserved.

A package inside this monorepo is installed from git with a `path:` parameter that belongs to the committish, as in `github:zhangj1164/dsh-mega-plugins#path:packages/memo/dsh-memo`, with a commit pinned as `#<sha>&path:packages/memo/dsh-memo`; an `&path:` written against the repository URL is taken as part of the repository name and fails as a missing repository.

A git install fetches source rather than build output, so `prepare` builds `lib/`; pnpm ≥10 refuses that build until the profile authorizes it (`ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`), the printed `allowBuilds` key names the resolved commit and stops matching after a push, and the durable repository-level key `'<package>@git+https://github.com/zhangj1164/dsh-mega-plugins.git': true` authorizes package code to run on the installing machine outside any agent sandbox.

A git-installed manifest keeps `workspace:^` in its sibling peer ranges because nothing rewrites a manifest read from a checkout; pnpm prints a peer warning and the boot is unaffected since the profile names every needed package and sets `autoInstallPeers: false`, while the registry stays the better default because a published package ships prebuilt `lib/` and needs no build authorization.

A bundle layer is composed at boot, so composing an unpublished build means running `pnpm run build`, installing the package directory with `dsh plugin --profile web add "link:<absolute package path>"`, and restarting the host; `patchReload: live` reloads configuration documents rather than modules, so a rebuilt `lib/` and a newly written `dsh.profile.bundles` row are both invisible to a running process.

`@zhangj1164/dsh-openwiki-visualize` is installed completely by naming that one package, because its single `openwiki-visualize` row carries both the host service and the browser half, whereas the memo suite requires five package names in one command.

Four of the five memo-suite names are the minimum for the dsh-memo bundle's two rows to resolve — `@zhangj1164/dsh-telemetry` and `@zhangj1164/dsh-github-issue` supply the injected `telemetry` and `githubIssue` services and `@zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo` is the package its `ui-memo` row names — while `@zhangj1164/dsh-client-ui-memo-settings` only adds the Settings page and can be added or removed without touching the memo bundle.

When the settings page does not appear after a restart, the documented check order is: the Host build carries `.volatile()` schema fields, `dsh --profile web --dump-config` lists a `ui-memo-settings` row (otherwise the package never became a profile layer), and the browser fetched `<package>/client.js`.

On success `verify-bundle-entries` prints the bundle count, `no duplicate entry id`, and one line listing every bundle with its inserted ids, so the gate output doubles as the current ownership listing; on failure it names each collision and which patch did not record the mutual exclusion.

Every patch in this repository only performs `insert`, and each inserted row is an entry id plus the package name plus that row's `config`; the package name is the host plugin entry imported at boot, and no patch writes `dsh.profile.bundles` itself, so which layers are enabled is decided only by the deployment profile.

The prose enumerations lag the manifests: `README.md`'s install section and `AGENTS.md`'s Bundle layers section name only the four bundles telemetry, github-issue, memo and ui-memo-settings, while a fifth package, `@zhangj1164/dsh-openwiki-visualize`, also declares `dsh.bundle` and appears only in `README.md`'s workspace-structure listing — so entry-id ownership has to be read from each manifest's `dsh.bundle.patch` and that patch.
